Container.Name: arr-mcp
Container.Overview: One MCP server for the whole *arr stack, so an AI assistant can answer the questions that live between services rather than inside one.[br][br] Speaks to Radarr, Sonarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, Jellyfin, Seerr, SABnzbd, Transmission and qBittorrent, correlates them on shared external ids, and answers things no single service can — "why isn't the film I requested on Tuesday showing up in Jellyfin?" walks the whole chain: requested, managed, indexed, downloaded, imported, scanned.[br][br] Configuration is a web page, not a YAML file: add your services from the UI, and it diagnoses each connection instead of printing pass/fail. Several Radarrs or Sonarrs are supported. Writes are off until you turn them on.[br][br] [b]Claim it before you expose the port.[/b] The first person to load the setup page chooses the username and password and owns the instance, so open the WebUI and claim it as soon as it starts.
Container.Changes: Template tracks the `latest` tag. Release notes: https://github.com/bardesss/arr-mcp/releases

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: The config UI and the MCP endpoint. Claim the instance before this port is reachable from anywhere you do not trust.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Holds config.yaml, the audit log and the optional IMDb dataset.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id that owns the appdata share. 99 is Unraid's `nobody`.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id that owns the appdata share. 100 is Unraid's `users`.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam. Affects timestamps in the audit log and the log viewer.
